newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris court convicts suspected Turkish guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Paris court convicts suspected Turkish guerrillas.

text.p: A French criminal court on Thursday sentenced a suspected member of the far-left Turkish Dev Sol guerrilla movement in his absence to four years in prison on terrorism charges.
Dursun Karatas, 43, a Dev Sol founder, was one of 11 alleged members of the group tried in the French capital last month.
Arrested during a routine border check in 1994, Karatas fled France after being released on bail the following year.
His controversial release by a Paris appeals court followed threats by the group to launch further attacks on French soil and target investigating magistrate Jean-Francois Ricard.
The 10 others on trial, including one other in absentia, were given punishments ranging from a year's suspended sentence to four years in prison.
Among them was German journalist Ursula Hoppe-Unlu, who was given a 12-month suspended sentence and banned from the Paris area for three years.
During the trial she was described as a former member of the German leftist guerrilla movement the Red Army Faction.
But a French communist-controlled journalists' union said her only crime "was to have recorded the Turkish state's repression of democrats and Kurds".
Six German human rights activists on Wednesday filed suit "against themselves" in France to show their support for her.
They said she had met Dev Sol members only to inquire about their politics, adding that such activities were not punishable under German law.
During the trial prosecutor Anne Obez-Vosgien had demanded at least six years in prison for Karatas and sentences ranging from two to five years against the other defendants.
The specific charge against them was belonging to an illegal group engaged in terrorist activities.
French authorities accuse Dev Sol guerrillas of damaging Turkish property in Paris, Strasbourg and Lyon between 1981 and 1992 and extorting money from Turkish businesses.
Dev Sol, created in 1978, is held responsible in Turkey for the deaths of several hundred people, including the 1994 murder of Justice Minister Mehmet Topac.
